title: Reconciliation drift work claims are pruned once they can no longer be re-presented
problem_register_class: RC3 / WP3.1 (Unbounded or wasteful persistent writers — reconciliation_drift.work_claims)

writer_runtime_budget.writer: reconciliation_drift.work_claims (PostgreSQL JSONB owner store) and work_claims.json (JSON store fallback)

write_cadence.telemetry_consume: 1 claim per consumed telemetry event = 5,112 to 5,912 claims/day (hosted total 5,400 to 6,200 claims/day, ~6,000 claims/day average)

unbounded_state_before_fix.cleanup: none (completed and failed claims were retained indefinitely)

bounded_state_after_fix.cleanup_trigger: Executed automatically after each scheduled_reconcile tick in services/reconciliation-drift/main.py and directly via store.prune_work_claims()

AC1_bounded_cas_delete_with_configurable.details: Completed and failed scheduled_reconcile claims older than 24h and telemetry_consume claims older than 7d (both configurable via kwargs and env vars) are deleted in bounded batches using PostgresJsonOwnerStore.delete_if_matches / _delete_work_claim_if_matches.

AC2_live_lease_never_deleted.details: In-progress claims and claims holding a lease_token or active lease_expires_at are excluded from candidate selection; a failed claim concurrently recovered by a worker before delete_if_matches is protected by the CAS payload equality check (cas_conflict_count=1, deleted_count=0).

AC3_runtime_summary_and_consumer_state_p.details: Claims whose window_id is the current last_event_id or last_heartbeat_event_id of any listed runtime summary or is pending or dead-lettered in consumer state (ConsumerWorkerState or consumer-worker-state.json) are never deleted, preventing a stopped runtime's last event from being reprocessed into a duplicate drift report or incident.

AC4_re_presenting_pruned_window_after_ho.details: Re-presenting a pruned scheduled_reconcile window after its 24h horizon produces at most one new evaluation (0 for identical tick_id, 1 for a retry tick_id on the same window_id) and 0 duplicate incidents; re-presenting a pruned telemetry_consume event after its 7d horizon deduplicates against the persisted drift report and produces 0 duplicate incidents.

AC5_hosted_shape_growth_bound_and_150k_m.details: On 150,000 existing completed claims at hosted shape (6,000 claims/day = 288 scheduled_reconcile + 5,712 telemetry_consume over 25 days), pruning deletes 109,728 expired claims in 22 bounded batches and leaves 40,272 steady-state rows (<= 45,000 cap), holding steady at 40,272 rows on subsequent 6,000-claim days.

AC6_rollback_compatibility.details: The previous accepted release store loaded from ede3b8035:services/reconciliation-drift/store.py reads surviving completed receipts, respects surviving active leases, and acquires/completes pruned windows without schema or payload changes.

residual_findings.problem_register_class: RC3 / WP3.2 (Storage manifest and writer bounds)
residual_findings.finding: Sibling authority tables in PostgresReconciliationDriftStore (especially drift_evaluations, written once per active binding per 5-minute scheduled tick) do not yet declare a retention horizon or pruning job; should be inventoried under WP3.2 storage manifest.
